name: task
description:
Hand a self-contained piece of work to a subagent, which works on its own and returns only its final report — keeping the searching and reading out of your context.

- Use it for broad research ("where is X handled, and what calls it?") or a separable job. For one file you already know, just read it.
- `prompt` must stand on its own: the subagent sees nothing of this conversation. Say what to find or do, and what to report back.
- Independent tasks can run in the same turn. Subagents that change files at the same time should each have `worktree: true`, so they work on separate branches.
- Agents: {{agents}}

worktree.description: Work in a separate git checkout on a new branch, apart from yours — for changes made alongside other work; the result says how to merge it

model.description: Run it on another configured model (connection/model, from the list in your instructions) — a second opinion, or a model better at this kind of work. Default: the agent's own model, else yours.

variables.agents: the subagents a task may name: `name — description`, separated by "; "
